answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it can claim rewards, then slash that stake when independent audits catch duplicate or fabricated behavior. Auditors sample claims and compare signed interaction histories, so merely minting more keys does not multiply influence. A real participant can recover the stake by behaving consistently; an attacker must lock up capital for every identity and risks losing it. Even a tundra courier using a quill to record a whisper leaves costly, auditable traces.
